edges.description: Mite products and keratinocyte/fibroblast chemokines recruit neutrophils, macrophages, T lymphocytes, eosinophils, and mast cells into the dermis.
Keratinocyte and fibroblast cytokines and chemokines (including IL-1alpha, IL-1beta, and CXCL8) recruit neutrophils, macrophages, T cells, and eosinophils to the dermis.

edges.description: Secreted epidermal and dermal cytokines engage cell-surface receptors to activate intracellular JAK-STAT signaling cascades in lesional skin.
edges.source: Keratinocyte and Fibroblast Cytokine and Keratinization Response

edges.description: Sustained upregulation of epidermal keratinization programs and keratinocyte-derived IL-20 signaling drives epidermal thickening, scaling, and hyperkeratotic crust formation in crusted scabies.
edges.source: Keratinocyte and Fibroblast Cytokine and Keratinization Response

edges.description: Infiltrating T cells, eosinophils, and mast cells secrete type 2 and pruritogenic cytokines including IL-4, IL-13, and IL-31.
edges.target: Type 2 Cytokine and IL-31 Pruritogenic Signaling

edges.description: Combined type I and delayed type IV dermal cellular infiltration produces erythematous papules and inflammatory skin lesions.
JAK-STAT pathway activation transduces and amplifies IL-4, IL-13, and IL-31 cytokine signaling in lesional skin.
edges.target: Type 2 Cytokine and IL-31 Pruritogenic Signaling

edges.description: Elevated IL-4, IL-13, and IL-31 in lesional skin directly stimulate and sensitize cutaneous sensory nerve fibers to produce intense pruritus.
edges.source: Type 2 Cytokine and IL-31 Pruritogenic Signaling

edges.description: Scratching induced by intense pruritus breaches the epidermal barrier, facilitating secondary bacterial skin and soft-tissue infections.
Epidermal burrows and inflammatory skin lesions disrupt skin barrier integrity and predispose to bacterial superinfection (impetigo).

nodes.description: Recruitment and accumulation of T lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils, eosinophils, and mast cells in the dermis. In ordinary scabies, CD4+ T lymphocytes predominate in a 4:1 ratio over CD8+ T cells as part of a protective Th1 cell-mediated response, whereas crusted scabies exhibits dermal CD8+ T-cell predominance alongside heavy eosinophil, lymphocyte, and macrophage infiltration.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: Upon recruitment to infection site/draining lymph nodes, eosinophils, mast cells, and basophils produce IL-4 and /or IL-13 (10). In a study reported by Walton et al. in 2008, skin biopsies taken from scabies patients having crusted lesions showed large numbers of lymphocytes, monocytes, macrophages, and eosinophils in the dermis, with increased levels of IgE in the blood samples.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: The immune response to S. scabiei consistently shows increased levels of CD4+ or CD8+ T cells. CD4+ T cells mostly dominate the infiltrates of skin biopsy lesions in ordinary scabies, with a 4:1 ratio of CD4+ to CD8+ T cells (12, 13).

nodes.description: Marked epidermal thickening with exuberant, scaly, hyperkeratotic crusted plaques teeming with mites, characteristic of crusted (Norwegian) scabies.

evidence.reference_title: An Itchy Problem: A Clinical Case of Crusted Scabies.
evidence.snippet: The immunophenotyping study was inconclusive and histological examination of the skin revealed marked hyperkeratosis with abundant arthropod parasites compatible with S. scabiei (Fig. 3).

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: IL-20 is also a proinflammatory cytokine produced by keratinocytes, monocytes, and endothelial cells and is associated with epidermal thickening, scales, and crusts in CS (19, 99).

nodes.description: Transcriptional and functional upregulation of the intracellular JAK-STAT signaling cascade in scabies-infested skin, promoting macrophage and neutrophil activation, B- and T-lymphocyte differentiation, and amplification of cytokine-mediated cutaneous inflammation.

biological_processes: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: The clustering patterns showed various differentially expressed genes including inflammatory responses and innate immunity genes (DEFB4A, IL-19, CXCL8, CSF3, SERPINB4, S100A7A, HRNR) and notably upregulation of the JAK-STAT pathway in scabies-infested samples.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: Differentially expressed genes that were enhanced in OS included immune-related signaling pathways and JAK-STAT pathways. Their impacts include activation of macrophages and neutrophils, host inflammatory responses, and the differentiation of B and T cells, which control the wound repair (67).

nodes.description: Epidermal keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts respond to burrowing mites by upregulating innate proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines (including IL1A, IL1B, and CXCL8) alongside epidermal development and keratinization gene programs (including KRT6C, KRT9, SPRR2A, SPRR3, and LCE3A).
nodes.id: Keratinocyte and Fibroblast Cytokine and Keratinization Response

evidence.reference_title: Sarcoptes scabiei mites modulate gene expression in human skin equivalents.
evidence.snippet: Genes for the expression of interleukin-1α (IL-1α) precursor, IL-1β, granulocyte/macrophage-colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) precursor, and G-CSF precursor were up-regulated 2.8- to 7.4-fold, paralleling cytokine secretion profiles. A large number of genes involved in epithelium development and keratinization were also differentially expressed in response to live scabies mites.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: Top upregulated genes displayed a role in inflammatory responses and innate immunity (DEFB4A, IL-19, CXCL8, CSF3, SERPINB4, S100A7A, HRNR), keratinization (KRT9, KRT6C, EGR4, SPRR3, LCE3A, SPRR2A, LCE3A), and a gene involved in desquamation processes in skin (SPINK9);

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: As expected, the results showed that pathways associated with skin development, including keratinization, epidermis development, and keratinocyte differentiation, were highly upregulated in the diseased samples.

nodes.description: Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis burrows into the stratum corneum of human epidermis and feeds on host epidermis and sera, releasing antigenic saliva, fecal pellets, and active metabolites that disrupt the epidermal barrier and initiate host cutaneous inflammatory and immune responses.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: S. scabiei var. hominis causes skin infestation in humans by forming burrows in the stratum corneum of the skin and feeding on host epidermis and sera. The release of active metabolites from the mite contribute to the intense itching and inflammation manifesting as a skin allergy and inflammatory responses (2). Potential sources of allergens include fecal material, mite bodies, mite saliva secreted at feeding, soluble proteins released after death in body fluids, and enzymes involved in molting and digestive processes (34).

evidence.reference_title: An Itchy Problem: A Clinical Case of Crusted Scabies.
evidence.snippet: Scabies is an infestation of the skin by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei.

nodes.description: Systemic antiparasitic pharmacotherapy administered as two oral doses of ivermectin (200 ug/kg given 7 to 14 days apart because ivermectin is not ovicidal) for individual case management, crusted scabies combination regimens, and community-wide mass drug administration (MDA) in endemic settings.

evidence.reference_title: A framework for scabies control
evidence.snippet: The recommended regimen for MDA is 2 doses of oral ivermectin (200 μg/kg) given 7 to 14 days apart, using directly observed treatment wherever possible.

evidence.reference_title: Scabies: update on treatment and efforts for prevention and control in highly endemic settings.
evidence.snippet: Mass treatment with permethrin cream or ivermectin can be given directly to patients.

nodes.description: Intense generalized or localized itching, characteristically worse at night, resulting from host type I and type IV hypersensitivity responses and IL-4/IL-31 pruritogenic signaling in response to burrowing mites and their antigens.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: Infestation by the mite almost always leads to the development of localized skin inflammation, itching, and burrow formation; rash and itch possibly being an indicator of host immune response with features of both type I and type IV hypersensitivity reactions (6).

evidence.reference_title: An Itchy Problem: A Clinical Case of Crusted Scabies.
evidence.snippet: The authors describe a clinical case of crusted scabies with pruritus and exuberant cutaneous lesions.

nodes.description: Secondary bacterial skin and soft-tissue infections, most commonly superficial impetigo caused by Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus entering through mite burrows and excoriations, which can progress to severe soft-tissue infection, invasive sepsis, or post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis in endemic settings.

evidence.reference_title: A framework for scabies control
evidence.snippet: Scabies is a strong risk factor for superficial bacterial skin infection (impetigo), which can progress to severe bacterial infections, poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, and possibly acute rheumatic fever and chronic kidney disease

nodes.description: Inflammatory cutaneous eruption with burrows, erythematous papules, and excoriations in ordinary scabies, or exuberant psoriasiform plaques in crusted scabies.

nodes.description: Upregulation of type 2 cytokines (IL4, IL13) and the pruritogenic cytokine IL31, alongside Th2-associated chemokines (CCL17, CCL18), in mite-infested skin. IL-4 sensitizes pruriceptors to histamine and IL-31 signals to induce severe pruritus, with expression levels correlating directly with clinical itch severity scores.
nodes.id: Type 2 Cytokine and IL-31 Pruritogenic Signaling

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: DEGs in scabies mite-infested skin included those encoding certain chemokines (C-C motif) ligands CCL2, CCL17, and CCL 18, (C-X-C motif) ligand CXCL1, IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-23, IL-31 with FC greater than two for most of the genes. IL-4, CCL7, CCL20, IL-19, IL-20, IL-36A were also prominent DEGs with high FCs that were significantly correlated with the itch severity scores.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: Marked enrichment of immune response pathways (JAK-STAT signaling, IL-4 and IL-13 pathway, and Toll receptor cascade), chemokine ligands and receptors (CCL17, CCL18, CCL3L1, CCL3L3, CCR7), and cytokines (IL-13 and IL-20) were observed.

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptome Analysis of Host Inflammatory Responses to the Ectoparasitic Mite Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis.
evidence.snippet: IL-4 and IL-31 were also significantly high in scabies mite-infested skin. IL-4 is reported to increase the itching even in low dose of histamine (91), and IL-31 is known to be involved in causing itching by signal activation of IL-13 receptors, but the mechanism involved is still unclear (92).
